deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of Riemann's 1860 memoir 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite'. The draft treats the isothermal (Boyle) gas, pressure = a^2*rho, in one space dimension. The published paper calls the Riemann invariants r and s; here they are called p and q. The previous page works with combinations of log(rho) and x'/a.

(1) The setting, in modern form. The equations are rho_t + (rho*u)_x = 0 and u_t + u*u_x + a^2*rho_x/rho = 0. They can be written in characteristic (Riemann-invariant) form using u + a*log(rho) and u - a*log(rho). These are transported along dx/dt = u + a and dx/dt = u - a respectively.

(2) Normalisation of p and q (my inference). The page does not define p and q. With p and q proportional to (log(rho) + u/a) and (log(rho) - u/a), the velocity u is proportional to a*(p - q) and log(rho) to p + q. The page states two propagation speeds:
- a value of p moves toward larger x with speed a*(p - q + 1/2);
- a value of q moves toward smaller x ('in entgegengesetzter Richtung') with speed a*(q - p + 1/2), i.e. dx/dt = a*(p - q - 1/2).
These are the two characteristic speeds u ± a, written in rescaled invariants. One consistent choice is p = (log(rho) + u/a)/4 and q = (log(rho) - u/a)/4, so that u = 2a(p - q). Then u ± a = 2a(p - q ± 1/2). This matches the page up to a global factor of 2, which can be absorbed into the time unit. With the plain choice p, q = (log(rho) ± u/a)/2 one would instead get a(p - q ± 1).

(3) Qualitative argument (heavily revised; the final version survives). The p-wave speed a(p - q + 1/2) increases with p. In a disturbance of finite extent, every value of p eventually meets the same set of q values, though at different times. Hence 'a larger value of p will on average advance with greater speed than a smaller one.' The page breaks off at 'als ein kleinerer'.

(4) Purpose. This is the step toward the conclusion that forward-facing compression parts of the wave steepen: larger p overtakes smaller p. The solution then becomes multivalued, which in the memoir leads to the 'Verdichtungsstoss' (shock) discussion.

The struck-out lines are earlier attempts at the same sentence. No further computation is on the page.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. The speeds a(p-q±1/2) imply a normalisation of p and q that is not stated on the page. With p, q = (log rho ± u/a)/2 one would get a(p-q±1); the factor 1/2 is consistent only with p, q = (log rho ± u/a)/4 and time rescaled by 2, or an equivalent convention. Treat the normalisation as uncertain.

The 'on average' (durchschnittlich) argument is heuristic. It assumes every p value meets the same q values, which holds for a disturbance of compact support. Riemann does not make it quantitative here.

results.what: Characteristic speeds u±a of the isothermal 1-D Euler equations, expressed through Riemann invariants p, q (logarithmic in density)
results.modern_name: Riemann invariants / method of characteristics for 1-D gas dynamics

results.what: Argument that larger invariant values propagate faster on average, so the wave steepens
results.modern_name: Wave steepening / gradient catastrophe leading to shock formation

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of a sentence that appears nearly verbatim in Riemann's published 1860 Luftwellen memoir (there with r, s instead of p, q). Nothing new beyond the published work.

checkable.sympy: x,t,a=symbols('x t a',positive=True); rho=Function('rho')(x,t); u=Function('u')(x,t); rt=-diff(rho*u,x); ut=-u*diff(u,x)-a**2*diff(rho,x)/rho; R=u+a*log(rho); simplify(diff(u,x)*0 + (ut + a*rt/rho) + (u+a)*diff(R,x))
checkable.asserts: R = u + a*log(rho) satisfies R_t + (u+a)R_x = 0 for the isothermal Euler equations (expression simplifies to 0).

checkable.sympy: x,t,a=symbols('x t a',positive=True); rho=Function('rho')(x,t); u=Function('u')(x,t); rt=-diff(rho*u,x); ut=-u*diff(u,x)-a**2*diff(rho,x)/rho; S=u-a*log(rho); simplify((ut - a*rt/rho) + (u-a)*diff(S,x))
checkable.asserts: S = u - a*log(rho) satisfies S_t + (u-a)S_x = 0 (expression simplifies to 0).

checkable.sympy: a,rho,u=symbols('a rho u',positive=True); p=(log(rho)+u/a)/4; q=(log(rho)-u/a)/4; simplify((u+a) - 2*a*(p-q+Rational(1,2)))
checkable.asserts: With p, q = (log rho ± u/a)/4 the forward speed u+a equals 2a(p-q+1/2), the page's form up to a time-scale factor 2.

checkable.sympy: a,rho,u=symbols('a rho u',positive=True); p=(log(rho)+u/a)/4; q=(log(rho)-u/a)/4; simplify((u-a) + 2*a*(q-p+Rational(1,2)))
checkable.asserts: The backward speed u-a equals -2a(q-p+1/2): q values move toward smaller x with speed proportional to (q-p+1/2).
The p-wave speed is increasing in p (derivative a > 0), the basis of the steepening argument.

transcription_corrections: The first word 'Nachdem[?]' is uncertain; it may be a struck or faint start such as 'Es rückt' (the published text reads 'Es rückt also ein bestimmter Werth von r ... fort').
The insertion above line 2 is best read as 'in entgegengesetzter Richtung'. It replaces the struck 'zu kleinern Werthen' and is correctly placed after 'ein Werth von q'.
In line 1, 'bestimmter' appears struck through, consistent with the transcription.
The final legible line ends 'als ein kleinerer' with no full stop; the page breaks off there.
